short: DDSP prior and jointly trained vocoder (M06) are standard: joint waveform training predates it; quality leads its baselines, but LRS3 WER 30.4% trails the uncompared LipVoicer (21.4%).
position: NaturalL2S [@liang2025naturall2s] changes the waveform generator (M06), a DDSP harmonic-and-noise prior feeding a conditional HiFi-GAN trained jointly behind a frozen AV-HuBERT, and drops use-time speaker input (M07). Both are standard: joint end-to-end waveform generation for many speakers predates it, on word-level LRW and 33-speaker GRID [@mira2021endtoend; @um2021facetron], so the "first attempt" claim (§I) fails as worded, and reference-free use follows DiffV2S [@choi2023diffv2s]. The quality lead over the four compared systems (Tables I–III) recurs in a [later] same-group test [@liang2026sldl2s]. Content does not: LRS3 WER is 30.4%, behind Lip2Speech Unit (27.7%, Table II), as the authors concede (§V-B), and behind the cited but uncompared LipVoicer (21.4% under its own ASR) [@yemini2024lipvoicer]. The joint-training ablation also removes DDSP and changes the vocoder corpus, and removing DDSP alone lowers DNS-MOS only from 2.95 to 2.89 (Table IV), so the source of the gain is not isolated.
